mainEntity.name: Levitating Figure, known as ‘The Dreamer’
mainEntity.description:
Quentin Bell was the son of Vanessa and Clive Bell and nephew of Virginia Woolf. He is renowned as a ceramicist, and for his books on the Bloomsbury artists and a biography of Woolf. He was appointed Head of Fine Art at the University of Leeds in 1959, and later Professor of Fine Art, until 1967. In 1978, Stanley Burton suggested acquiring a work by Bell for the Leeds campus.

Bell proposed a levitating figure – a recurrent theme in his art inspired by a conjuror’s trick he saw as a child – and suggested six potential locations. Stanley and the Vice-Chancellor, Lord Boyle, eventually decided on a site near the Edward Boyle Library. The work was cast in fibreglass with a steel armature, in an inter-disciplinary partnership with the Department of Civil Engineering. Dr Gurdev Singh was responsible for the design and construction of the internal support and the Department oversaw the installation.

Unveiled by Stanley Burton in October 1982, it has moved several times. It was removed from its original site due to the Library’s expansion and re-sited in the quiet courtyard of the Baines Wing coffee bar, and has more recently been relocated to Clothworkers’ Court, so that it is more accessible to visitors. Commonly known on campus as ‘The Dreamer’, it is not clear when this title was acquired. It has also been called ‘The Astral Lady’, and Bell’s original notes refer to it as the ‘Elmdon Figure’. Whatever its title or location, the artwork is one of the most popular on campus, and has become a site for personal pilgrimages and memorials.
